results.title: Ample capacity: the constrained plan matches the unconstrained one
results.what: When no site's capacity ever binds, solving the LP should change nothing: every pack is delivered, and every site's load matches the lot-for-lot requirement plan exactly.

checks.name: load matches the requirement plan, max relative difference

results.title: A hard bottleneck: unmet demand equals the shortfall, exactly
results.what: Packaging capped at 800 of a 1,000-pack-a-month demand, with no stock, re-sourcing or other relief: delivered plus unmet must equal demand in every month, and delivered can never exceed capacity by even a rounding error.

checks.name: delivered + unmet = demand, every month, max error

results.title: Stock built ahead of a peak measurably improves service, as published
results.what: The README states two fill rates for the example network with fixed sourcing shares: 85.8% with no stock built ahead of a peak, 85.9% allowing up to 6 months. At a real holding cost the gain is small. Reproducing both from the same network confirms pre-building is doing real, bounded work — a modest, plausible gain, not a rounding artefact.

results.title: Priorities: a higher-priority market is protected first when capacity is short
results.what: Two markets share a capped warehouse; demand together exceeds capacity. Giving one market priority 3 against the other's 1 should concentrate the shortfall on the low-priority market.

checks.name: priority-1 market absorbs the shortfall (fill < priority-3's)

results.title: The published example reproduces its stated fill rate
results.what: The shipped example network (19 sites, 13-year horizon), solved within capacity with qualified-lane re-sourcing and 6 months of stock ahead allowed: the README states an 86.8% fill rate with the first unmet demand in December 2032.

results.title: Builds when the margin saved clearly beats the capex
results.what: A warehouse short by 300 packs/month at a $10/pack margin loses $3,000/mo in margin, every month, forever. A $1,000 candidate that closes the gap should obviously be built, immediately.

results.title: A budget cap picks the affordable option, not just the best one
results.what: Two candidates would each be worth building on their own; a budget too small for both should pick the cheaper one and stay under the cap, not round up and overspend.

results.title: The example network's investment decision is reproducible and proven optimal
results.what: The example network's four illustrative candidates (Jebel Ali, Cape Town Packaging, Valencia Dosing, Hamilton Nutrition), at the default pack value and discount rate: the optimiser should reach a provably optimal answer — not a timed-out guess — within well under a minute.

checks.name: investing improves fill over building nothing
capexTotal matches the sum of the chosen investments
